about: What Eyefinder knows about each game's files, read by ef_core::docs, the Documentation page and `eyefinder-cli docs`. MISSING.md is generated from the rows with status "missing". status: verified = output checked against real game files; spec = implemented from the cited specification, not yet confirmed on real files; documented = a specification exists but Eyefinder does not implement it; missing = no public documentation found. Every row cites its sources; real-file observations are recorded in docs/SUPPORT.md.

sections.title: PlayStation: GTA1, London 1969, GTA2
sections.intro: The releases are identified: disc serials come from redump, the boot rule from psx-spx (see [docs/FORMATS.md](docs/FORMATS.md#console-releases)). The CD audio tracks of GTA1 and London 1969 are decoded. Nothing else on these discs is documented.

sections.title: Dreamcast: GTA2
sections.intro: The disc is identified from IP.BIN, matched against redump's disc pages. The `.STR` audio streams are decoded, following vgmstream. The maintainer's disc (redump 19717, rebuilt as a DiscJuggler image) was compared file by file with the GTA2 PC release of 2004 (docs/SUPPORT.md): its maps are byte-identical and its styles use the PC format, so those are read with the PC readers.

sections.title: Game Boy Color: GTA1, GTA2
sections.intro: The ROMs are identified by cartridge header (Pan Docs) and by No-Intro SHA-1.

sections.title: Game Boy Advance: GTA Advance
sections.intro: The ROMs are identified by cartridge header (GBATEK game codes BGTE / BGTP) and by No-Intro SHA-1.

entries.known: Marschall's inventory: "RAT: 8-bit graphics that use the F_PAL.RAW palette", RAW are raw 640×480 frames, ACT is the "Photoshop ACT Format". London 1961's `f_logoe*.raw` are 24-bit only.
entries.needed: The dimensions of each file, and which palette goes with which image. Without them the pixels cannot be laid out without guessing.

entries.known: Marschall: "purpose unclear".
entries.needed: Everything.

entries.known: Marschall: KANJI.BIT holds 5040 glyphs of 16×16 pixels at 1 bit per pixel, and KANJI.IDX is an Int16 → Int16 table. The lookup index "becomes transformed (unknown)".
entries.needed: The index transform. FXT text shows Japanese characters as their Shift-JIS codes, and the glyphs are not drawn.

entries.data: FXT codes `0x00 xx yy` and `0xC3 xx`
entries.known: Marschall's converter keeps them as "illegal character" markers. His notes say `0x00` "is not found in the game files" and give only a theory for it.
entries.needed: What the game does with them. Eyefinder shows them as marked codes.

entries.known: DMA's CityScape document says 325 in §3.6 and 305 in §3.7. OpenGTA accepts 325.
entries.needed: Whether any release uses 305. Files with 305 are refused.

entries.known: The exe paths are known: `gtawin\gtawin.exe` (Classics / Steam), `GTAWIN\GRAND THEFT AUTO.EXE` and `GTADOS\GTA24.EXE`, `GTA8.EXE`, `GTAFX.EXE` (retail discs), `gtawin\gta_uk.exe`, `gtawin\gta_61.exe`. Retail PC discs are identified by their tracks against redump's PC DAT, and one disc executable is known from a real-file report.

entries.known: GTA2: DMA's GBH Style 4.6 describes a `PSXT` chunk (256×256 pages of 32×32 tiles, 15-bit BGR palettes). The document calls it a design that "may be scrapped".

entries.known: GTA2: GBH Map 8.2 describes a `PSXM` chunk and says the PSX version "must use CMAP in the final version". The PC and Dreamcast GMP files carry a 4096-byte `PSXM` chunk (2026-10-23).

entries.data: Which files are STR streams, and what they are
entries.known: vgmstream: "4-bit: common [GTA2 (DC)]". The maintainer's disc holds A, D, M, S1-S12 and S101 `.STR` at the root (2026-10-23).
entries.needed: Which streams are music and which are speech, and whether multi-track or 16-bit streams occur (Eyefinder decodes only single-track 4-bit streams and reports the others).

entries.known: The SDT files are the same 7680 bytes (320 slots of 24 bytes) as on PC, but every sample is about a quarter of the PC size (WIL slot 0: 59394 → 14852 bytes; radio slot 69: 2063 → 1032), i.e. 4 bits per sample (2026-10-23).
entries.needed: The codec. The Dreamcast's AICA ADPCM is likely but not documented for these banks, so they are not decoded.

entries.known: The files start with `GBIX` and contain a `PVRT` chunk (2026-10-23).
entries.needed: A cited PowerVR texture specification to decode them against.

entries.known: Each level folder (BIL, STE, WIL, FSTYLE) holds them (2026-10-23).
entries.needed: Everything.

entries.known: One 73,828,352-byte Sofdec-named file at the root (2026-10-23).
entries.needed: A cited specification of its container and codecs.

entries.data: Everything in the ROM (tiles, palettes, compression, maps, text, music sequencer, sound effects)
entries.known: Nothing GTA-specific. Only the generic Game Boy 2bpp tile format is public, and there is no evidence of how these ROMs store or compress their data.
entries.needed: Everything.

entries.data: Sprites, city textures, fonts, text, sound samples, music
entries.known: GTA-Advance-Studio (@ `7eae5b3e`) claims for the **European** ROM: "2,475 sprites (2,303 BIOS-RLE compressed, 172 uncompressed), 4bpp", "640 uncompressed 8-bit city textures", 8×8 4bpp fonts at fixed offsets, Latin-1 strings via pointers, and "282 PCM samples … 9,556 Hz, 8 bits, mono". It also says the ROM does **not** use a sequencer such as MusicPlayer2000.
entries.needed: All of it is found by scanning heuristics and fixed offsets in one ROM: no record boundaries or tables are documented (its notes say the ROM "does not reveal exactly where the logical record ends"). There is nothing for the USA ROM (BGTE). The no-sequencer claim is unconfirmed.

entries.confirmation: Maintainer's GTA2 PS1 VCD, 2026-10-23: header bytes as cue2pops writes them; identified as SLES-01404.

entries.data: CD audio tracks inside a VCD
entries.known: cue2pops stores them inline and writes their positions into the header.
entries.needed: A mapping from header to stream that holds for every converter option: cue2pops shifts the header times by its gap options and may inject a pregap (cue2pops.c lines 740-960), so Eyefinder reads only the data track of a VCD. Use the BIN/CUE for the music.
